description: Investigate the 11 patch scripts that exist in scripts/ but are neither documented in CLAUDE.md nor applied to the binary. Pure Read/Grep/Glob.

units.prompt:
READ-ONLY ANALYSIS. Do not modify anything, do not execute anything, do not run any script. You are reading Python source and reporting on it.

CONTEXT, established today and not up for re-derivation. The Mashed repo keeps a set of binary-modification scripts under scripts/ named patch_mashed_*.py. There are 21 of them. A byte-level comparison of original/MASHED.exe against original/MASHED.exe.unpatched shows 111 differing bytes in 14 clusters, and every cluster is accounted for by just NINE of those scripts: show_windowed, skip_audio_com, skip_selector, skip_controller_dialog, fix_camera_res, disable_log, fix_fopen, fix_joypad, skip_movies. A tenth, skip_intro, operates on .mpg data files rather than the executable. The remaining ELEVEN are therefore inert: they are not referenced in CLAUDE.md and their changes are demonstrably not present in the binary.

YOUR SCOPE: read these eleven files under scripts/ and report on each.
  patch_mashed_clean_exit.py
  patch_mashed_fix_movie_uaf.py
  patch_mashed_force_keyboard.py
  patch_mashed_heap_reserve.py
  patch_mashed_no_focus_pause.py
  patch_mashed_skip_intro_logos.py
  patch_mashed_skip_teardown.py
  patch_mashed_unlock_all.py
  patch_mashed_unlock_restore.py
  patch_mashed_unlock_tracks.py
  patch_mashed_skip_powerups.py   (this one is already known RETIRED; report it for completeness and confirm its refusal guard)

For EACH file report, strictly from what the source says:
1. PURPOSE, in one sentence, taken from its own docstring or header comment rather than inferred from the filename.
2. MECHANISM: which addresses it targets and what byte change it makes at each. Quote the addresses.
3. WHY IT IS NOT APPLIED, if the file itself says so. Many of these repos leave a note explaining a retirement, a supersession, or an experiment that failed. Quote it. If the file gives no reason, say NO REASON STATED rather than inventing one.
4. RISK CLASS, chosen from: SAFE-DEV (a debugging or convenience aid, reversible, no gameplay effect), GAMEPLAY-ALTERING (unlocks content or changes rules, so it would corrupt a faithful-behaviour reference), BOOT-CRITICAL (touches the boot chain, could break startup), or CHEAT/UNLOCK. Justify in one clause.
5. WHETHER IT LOOKS SUPERSEDED by one of the nine applied patches, naming which.
6. Does it have a --restore or un-apply path?

Then produce THREE grouped verdicts:
  A) Scripts that look genuinely useful for the CURRENT work and are safe. The project runs unattended game captures for a remote user, so anything affecting window focus, keyboard input, pausing when not focused, or clean shutdown is especially relevant -- call those out explicitly.
  B) Scripts that must NEVER be applied to original/MASHED.exe because they would compromise it as the diffing reference for faithful-behaviour verification. The unlock_* family is the obvious candidate; say plainly whether applying them would invalidate behavioural comparisons.
  C) Scripts that are dead, experimental, or superseded and should be considered for deletion or archival.

Finish with a single recommendation: if exactly one of these eleven were to be adopted, which, and why. Cite file:line throughout. NO-GUESSING: if a script's effect is not determinable from its source, write [UNCERTAIN] and state what is missing. Do NOT write any file.
